For years, the Epic Games Store has invested resources in back-end tooling and the overall developer experience. Now, we’re focused on delivering on our promise to players. 

Watch this session recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 and find out how the store is evolving into a player-centric, games-first social ecosystem.

From new features to long-overdue improvements, the Epic Games Store development team is moving quickly and cooking with gas. Press play to get a look at the 12-month roadmap.

Explore what the Epic Games Store can offer developers here: store.epicgames.com/distribution

author: Unreal Engine
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Chicago 2026, we cover the state of relevant systems in Unreal Engine that help you implement persistence and hydration.

Many game projects face similar challenges when it comes to world state persistence and gameplay performance in large worlds. When players return to an area, they expect the world to be in the same state as they left it. 

Reloading the world state needs to happen when loading a save file, when changing maps, and even within the same map when the player returns to a location that World Partition has streamed out. 

Keeping expensive faraway gameplay actors alive also leads to bad performance in a large, dense world. Persistence and hydration are two closely related aspects of level loading. Persistence refers to reloading map sections while restoring the modified world state and player data. Hydration refers to switching the representation of gameplay entities when they are far away from the player from fully featured actors
title: The Player Was Here: Persisting World State and Actor LOD Systems | Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
